\section*{Derivative scope register}
Inside the calibration scope, f is a differentiable scalar function of x. The result name is introduced only by the recorded equation.
The recorded relation is \(\phi=\frac{df}{dx}\).
A neighboring manufacturing scope uses unrelated names, so its measurements do not enter this definition.

# Coupled force boundary note

This local block calls q a scalar charge and E the electric field sampled for a force estimate. It does not state whether magnetic-force terms are negligible or whether the field is evaluated at the body's center.

The recorded relation is $\omega=qE$.

A mechanics block elsewhere balances total force and acceleration, but that separate scope is not imported here.

\section*{Collection overlap comparison}
The local glossary calls A and B collections but leaves open whether they are ordinary sets or events in a probability space. The result name is introduced by the equation.
The recorded relation is \(\xi=A\cap B\).
No surrounding scope supplies a universe or a sample space, so the two readings remain live.

# Terminal-reference comparison

The worksheet assigns V and I to opposing terminal reference directions and explicitly says that no sign conversion has been applied. The result name is introduced by the equation.

The recorded relation is $\psi=VI$.

Thus the stated references contradict the common sign convention required for the product.

\section*{Mixer-chain scratchpad}
A preprocessing chain combines an area reading A and a velocity reading v with the private diamond operator. The document never defines that operator.
The recorded relation is \(\upsilon=A\diamond v\).
Because multiplication is not asserted, the chain does not state a cataloged flow-rate relation.

# Descent-step derivation

For one unconstrained update, x and the next iterate are vectors in the same space, g is the objective gradient there, and alpha is a scalar step size. The next iterate is named only by the equation.

The recorded relation is $\gamma=x-\alpha g$.

The subtraction therefore records one complete gradient-descent step.

\section*{Wall-rate calculation chain}
The calculation binds k to conductivity, A to wall area, Delta T to the face-temperature difference, and L to thickness. It does not establish steady one-dimensional conduction, constant conductivity, or absence of internal generation.
The recorded relation is \(\theta=\frac{kA\Delta T}{L}\).
The algebraic rate is recorded, but its required conduction regime is incomplete.

# Transport-product derivation

The derivation calls m a measured magnitude and u a motion-rate reading, without deciding whether m is mass or force. The left-hand response is likewise unlabeled.

The recorded relation is $\lambda=mu$.

The product can therefore denote momentum or mechanical power under two unresolved role assignments.

\section*{Nondifferentiable guard record}
The premise states that f is nowhere differentiable at the selected x, while the equation presents a first derivative value there. The result name is introduced by the equation.
The recorded relation is \(\sigma=\frac{df}{dx}\).
The premise directly contradicts the differentiability condition for this relation.

# Thermofluid sampling guard

A heated-loop estimate identifies rho_f as density and A as a section area, but v is only a point sensor reading. The note does not establish an area-mean normal velocity or a uniform profile.

The recorded relation is $\mu=\rho_f A v$.

The mass-flow product is structurally present while its sampling guard remains unverified.

\section*{Finite-graph degree audit}
For a finite undirected graph, kappa is explicitly the sum of all vertex degrees and E is its edge set. The equation records the certified count.
The recorded relation is \(\kappa=2|E|\).
Both roles belong to that same graph, satisfying the declared-domain guard.

# Field-glyph guard note

A lab shorthand combines electric-field and magnetic-field readings with a heart operator. No definition, time derivative, circulation, or sign convention is supplied for that glyph.

The recorded relation is $\delta=E\heartsuit B$.

The expression therefore does not state Faraday induction or another cataloged field law.

\section*{Unresolved A-v reference}
The preceding discussion calls A an operator-or-area entry and v a vector-or-velocity entry; the nouns are deliberately unresolved. The response name is introduced by the equation.
The recorded relation is \(\eta=Av\).
The formula can be a matrix-vector application or an area-times-velocity flow relation.

# Binary-loss pronoun ledger

In this model-card paragraph, y refers to the declared binary label and p refers to its predicted probability strictly between zero and one. The loss value is named only by the equation.

The recorded relation is $\chi=-[y\log p+(1-y)\log(1-p)]$.

Those references bind every role and establish the binary cross-entropy expression.

\section*{Material-reference heat note}
The memo identifies m as specimen mass, c as its tabulated specific heat, and Delta T as the measured interval. It does not say c stays constant across that interval or that no phase change occurs.
The recorded relation is \(\tau=mc\Delta T\).
The sensible-heat roles resolve, but the material-regime requirement remains open.

# Indefinite-factor reference

Here rho refers to the matrix previously declared nonsymmetric and indefinite, while L is labeled lower triangular. The equation claims the displayed factorization.

The recorded relation is $\rho=LL^{T}$.

The matrix declaration contradicts the positive-definite source requirement for Cholesky factorization.

\section*{Triangle-integral collision}
The black triangle is a locally invented separator inside an integration recipe. The author gives it no mathematical definition and does not claim a derivative relation.
The recorded relation is \(\nu=\int f(x)\blacktriangle dx\).
No public law assigns semantic authority to this composite operator.

# Power-product symbol collision

The imported columns V and I are only described as a driving quantity and a motion quantity. Their types do not decide whether V is voltage with I current or V is force with I velocity.

The recorded relation is $\zeta=VI$.

Accordingly the product admits electric-power and mechanical-power readings without a discriminator.

\section*{Union-glyph procedure collision}
The source explicitly declares A and B to be ordered procedures rather than sets, and it defines the union glyph here as sequential concatenation. The response is named by the equation.
The recorded relation is \(\beta=A\cup B\).
Those declarations contradict the set-domain meaning required by set union.

# Club-gradient collision

A transcription uses a club between the gradient mark and E, but never defines the club as a dot product, divergence, or another operator. Charge density and permittivity are absent.

The recorded relation is $\varepsilon=\nabla\clubsuit E$.

The line therefore cannot assert Gauss electric law.

\section*{Tank-state revision earlier draft}
Before agitation, the tank was settled and the fluid was at rest with constant density.
The recorded relation is \(p_h=\rho_fgh\).
This earlier draft recorded a hydrostatic pressure difference.

\section*{Tank-state revision}
After the revision, the tank is explicitly accelerating and the fluid is not at rest, although rho_f, g, and h retain their density, gravity, and depth meanings. The pressure difference is named by the equation.
The recorded relation is \(\vartheta=\rho_fgh\).
The edited operating state contradicts the hydrostatic-regime guard.

# Descent-shape revision earlier draft

The draft listed z, g, and eta_s without any shape or role declarations.

The recorded relation is $w_1=z-\eta_s g$.

Review requested explicit compatibility evidence.

# Descent-shape revision

The accepted revision declares z and the next iterate as vectors in one parameter space, g as the objective gradient in that space, and eta_s as a scalar step. The next iterate is named only by the equation.

The recorded relation is $\varpi=z-\eta_s g$.

The shape correction establishes a complete gradient-descent update.

\section*{Wall-model revision earlier draft}
The first draft contained an unlabeled proportionality with no material or geometry roles.
The recorded relation is \(r_w=kA/L\).
Review requested a temperature difference and explicit role bindings.

\section*{Wall-model revision}
The revised sheet now binds k to conductivity, A to normal area, Delta T to the wall-face difference, and L to thickness. It still says nothing about steadiness, dimensionality, property constancy, or internal generation.
The recorded relation is \(\varsigma=\frac{kA\Delta T}{L}\).
The edit supplies the roles but leaves the conduction-regime guard incomplete.

# Period-parameter revision earlier draft

The draft called T a positive timing value but did not tie it to any signal.

The recorded relation is $f_0=1/T$.

Review requested an identity decision for T.

# Period-parameter revision

The revised paragraph says T may be the measured period of the oscillator or a nondimensional tuning horizon; the editor has not chosen between those meanings. The response is named by the equation.

The recorded relation is $\aleph=1/T$.

Only the period reading supports frequency reciprocity, so the formula remains ambiguous.
